verdict: Church & Dwight's sales rose just 1% to $1,602M as last year's portfolio exits masked 5.1% organic growth, but wider margins lifted profit 16% to $212M.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: $1,602M vs $1,586M a year ago; organic sales +5.1%

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $0.75 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $0.92

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: up 170 basis points vs a year ago

kpis.label: Cash from operations
kpis.note: in Q3 alone; about $1.175B expected for the full year

segments.name: Consumer Domestic
segments.note: US household and personal-care brands — ARM & HAMMER laundry and cat litter, THERABREATH, WATERPIK and OXICLEAN. Reported sales rose just 0.4%, but organic sales grew 4.4% once portfolio exits are stripped out.

segments.name: Consumer International
segments.note: The same brands sold outside the US. Reported sales up 2.5%; organic sales up 7.8% on higher volume, led by THERABREATH, BATISTE, TOUCHLAND and OXICLEAN.

segments.name: Specialty Products
segments.note: Specialty chemicals and animal-productivity products, mainly for farms and industry. Sales up 5.0%, all of it organic.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Advertising and promoting the brands — 11.9% of sales, down from 12.8% a year ago.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company. Includes $6M of charges for restricted stock issued for the TOUCHLAND acquisition; adjusted SG&A was $261M.

otherDetail: Other expense, net was $22M, partly offset by $3M of equity earnings from affiliates — a net $19M drag below operating profit.
oneTimers: SG&A includes $6M of charges for restricted stock issued for the TOUCHLAND acquisition. Excluding that and similar items, adjusted operating income was $298M and adjusted EPS was $0.92, vs $0.89 on a GAAP basis.
footerNote: Figures are rounded to $M from the reported tenths, so rounded lines may differ by $1M from the printed statements.

takeaways.title: Organic growth beat the headline
takeaways.text: Reported sales rose only 1.0% to $1,602M because last year's strategic portfolio actions removed whole product lines. Organic sales — the brands Church & Dwight still owns — grew 5.1%, with volume up 4.6%, well ahead of the company's 3% outlook, and all three divisions grew.

takeaways.title: Margins widened sharply
takeaways.text: Gross margin rose 170 basis points to 46.8%, helped by higher volume, productivity, tariff refunds and a richer mix from acquisitions and portfolio actions, which more than offset inflation and transport costs. That margin gain is the main reason profit grew 16% on 1% sales growth.

takeaways.title: Outlook raised for the year
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS was $0.92, up 13.6%. The company raised its 2026 outlook to about 0.5% reported sales growth and about 5% organic growth, tightened adjusted EPS growth to about 7%, and approved a new $1B share repurchase program.
